response.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX,
           AVG(l.ALB) AS avg_alb,
           AVG(1.0 * l.UN / NULLIF(l.`T-BIL`, 0)) AS avg_un_tbil_ratio
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
), sex_averages AS (
    SELECT SEX,
           AVG(avg_alb) AS avg_alb,
           AVG(avg_un_tbil_ratio) AS avg_un_tbil_ratio
    FROM patient_averages
    GROUP BY SEX
), overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_sex_avg_alb
    FROM sex_averages
)
SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb, s.avg_un_tbil_ratio,
       s.avg_alb - o.mean_sex_avg_alb AS above_mean
FROM sex_averages AS s
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE s.avg_alb > o.mean_sex_avg_alb;

assumptions.assumption: A patient is included at the patient-averaging stage when they have at least one matched laboratory record; SQL AVG ignores null measurements and ratios, and a zero T-BIL makes that test's ratio undefined.
